newsitem.title: FRANCE: French shares close 2.02 pct up at historic high.
newsitem.headline: French shares close 2.02 pct up at historic high.

text.p: French shares ended 2.02 percent higher on an historic closing high on Wednesday after a strong rally on the back of recent opinion polls which took away uncertainty about the upcoming elections.

Dealers said that recent polls showed a clear majority of the ruling centre-right coalition in the May 25, June 1 two-round parliamentary elections, after a series of previous polls which showed a neck-to-neck tie.
Wall Street gains on the back of lower-than-expected U.S. April producer price inflation also boosted the French market.
The CAC-40 closed 55.05 points up at 2,774.63.
The intra-day high was set at 2,781.87. The previous closing high was set on Tuesday but the all-time intraday record dated from March 11, 1997.
The May future was 55 points higher at 2,764 francs.
Dealers said the stronger dollar also underpinned shares. Volume was 10.8 billion francs of which 8.4 billion in blue-chip shares.
Market economists said that the outlook for the French market was mixed, the only certainty being that it would be volatile. The share market is expected to react to any opinion poll news.
"We could go to the 2,800 very quickly. There is a strong buy side out there, a lot of liquidity is coming into the market. It is not just arbitrage," a dealer said.
"But people are underestimating the election risk, we're getting into an increasingly volatile and dangerous market," he added.
Thursday's U.S. consumer price index is also important.

Total, up 4.43 percent at 542 francs, was one of the biggest risers on Wednesday and had the highest individual turnover. Dealers said the stock was boosted by firmer oil prices and expectations chairman Thierry Desmarest will paint a bullish picture on the group's outlook at the general meeting of May 21.
Elf-Aquitaine, up 2.04 percent at 600 francs, also boosted. U.S. interest seen in oil stocks.
Alcatel Alsthom, up 3.14 percent at 689 francs, continues Tuesday rally on firmer first quarter sales with recovery in telecoms.
